answer: I'd like to talk about the first thing I ever built with my own hands. Something I once made myself that I am quite proud of was a small wooden shelf for my room. I had never really done any woodwork before, so it was genuinely [[ambitious]] for a complete beginner. I watched a few online tutorials, gathered some basic tools and set to work, expecting disaster. I bought a few planks from a carpenter's workshop near our local market and borrowed a saw and a drill from my father, who still keeps a box of tools from his business days. I measured everything on our balcony floor, cut the pieces, screwed them together and sanded the edges. The process was far more [[challenging]] than I anticipated, involving plenty of mistakes and a couple of bruised fingers. It was very much a case of [[trial and error]]. But I persevered, and after a weekend of effort, I had a shelf that actually stood up straight. I made it mainly because my books had outgrown the space on my desk, and I liked the idea of building something myself for once. The sense of [[satisfaction]] I felt was surprisingly intense, far greater than simply buying one. What made it special was that I had created something functional with my own two hands. Honestly, there is a unique pride that comes from making something yourself. It now sits in my room holding my books, and every time I look at it, I feel a little glow of accomplishment. It gave me a real appreciation for the value of [[craftsmanship]].

followUps.q: Have you made anything else since then?
followUps.answer: Only small things, like a wooden stand for my phone and a simple frame for a family photo. Nothing ambitious, but each project has made me a little more confident with tools.

followUps.q: Do you think people make fewer things by hand nowadays?
followUps.answer: I think so. Everything is so cheap and easy to order online that making things yourself can seem pointless, although I think it's a [[dying art]] that is well worth reviving.
